Reason: The ultrasound images demonstrate a cystic lung lesion in the fetus (Figure 1) with a distinct systemic feeding vessel visualized on color Doppler (Figure 2, arrow), which is the pathognomonic radiological sign of pulmonary sequestration. While the option mentions "large cystic lesions" and a "chest X-ray" (likely referring to the prenatal imaging context or postnatal confirmation), the presence of vascular flow definitively distinguishes this from CCAM/CPAM types II and III, which typically lack a systemic arterial supply.
